description: Resilient VI is the website of the U.S. Virgin Islands Hazard Mitigation and Resilience Plan; the plan page notes that FEMA requires public comments on the plan for its implementation. The pages read on 2026-09-28 offer hazard maps and a report repository. The maps page lists an interactive map of all hazards and maps of 10-year and 100-year return period hurricane winds, 475-year and 2,475-year earthquake hazard, landslide, NOAA sea level rise, rain-driven flooding, tsunami and wildfire. The repository gathers sector technical reports and two-page summaries for energy, water, health, telecommunications, transportation logistics and solid waste, a preliminary assessment of interdependent infrastructure resilience, operational models of the islands' interdependent water and power systems and of the critical supply chain for St Thomas and St John, studies of cell phone network resilience and synthetic internet networks, the 2040 transportation master plan and the 2014 and 2019 hazard mitigation plans. Coverage is the U.S. Virgin Islands. The PDFs are free to download and no licence is stated. Caveats: the map files were not opened, so whether the hazard layers can be downloaded as GIS data is unconfirmed, and several repository items are external reference reports. It supports island infrastructure resilience studies, such as combining hurricane wind maps with the water and power interdependency models. No related U.S. Virgin Islands infrastructure record is catalogued.
